newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slightly weaker, interest lacking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slightly weaker, interest lacking.

text.p: Singapore shares opened lower on Tuesday with interest switching to other regional markets, dealers said.
"There's no interest in coming into Singapore at the moment. All the funds are going elsewhere," a local dealer said.
Thailand was seen as the main beneficiary.
"Despite the systemic problems, the Thai stock market looks quite favourable for some short term gain and funds are being diverted there," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
At 0240 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was down 2.22 at 2,133.01.
Further sideways or consolidating moves were seen for Singapore in coming months.
"There's very little in the short term to lift us and we're looking some way ahead before liquidity returns," a dealer said.
Volume was slim, with 42.1 million shares changing hands by 0240 GMT, producing 113 gainers and 91 losers.

North Borneo Timbers surged early to head the gainers, rising Singapore $0.30 to S$9.45 Losers were led by DBS Bank foreign shares, down S$0.30 at S$17.70. Early actives were topped by Monday's new listing, Gul Technologies.
